experiment: LE1 — why light emerges, and whether heat alone or straight (directed) motion of a charge gives gamma-like light and electricity
inputs: whitepaper light chain as coded in legacy chemistry v1.0 (vp_light_emergence.py PART1-5, vp_light_angle.py): c^2 = B/rho single surviving wave; D = 2 lambda_C,e; propagation angle sin(chi) = lambda/(m D), m = ceil(lambda/D). Observations: Wien law, Planck spectrum, bremsstrahlung endpoint lambda_min = hc/eV (Duane-Hunt), annihilation line 511 keV.

predictions.P1_threshold: the near-longitudinal regime (m = 1, chi < 90 deg with lambda < D) begins exactly at photon energy hc/D = m_e c^2 / 2 = 255.5 keV (algebraic, given D = 2 lambda_C)
predictions.P2_heat_needs: for the Wien peak of thermal light to reach chi <= 45 deg needs T >= 8e8 K; at 3000 K the fraction of thermal photons with lambda < D is below 1e-100
predictions.P3_straight_motion: one electron accelerated in a straight line through V volts gives photons down to lambda_min = hc/eV; chi(lambda_min) <= 45 deg needs V ~ 0.36 MV (about 1e6 times less 'temperature-equivalent' energy concentration than heat: eV vs kT at 8e8 K ~ 69 keV per quantum but spread over all quanta)
predictions.P4_annihilation: e+e- annihilation photons (511 keV) have lambda = D/2 -> m = 1, chi = 30 deg
predictions.P5_direction: thermal emission has zero net momentum flux (isotropic) at every temperature; a direction exists only when a charge moves in a straight line (or a field/junction imposes one)
